requirements.evidence: Every contract member is present. Queues.php has all 8 properties and 15 methods; render passes accessQueue/accessGrants, scoped with find() and an empty collect() when null (Queues.php:235-243). Rename re-derives the slug: `slug: Str::slug($this->renameName)` (Queues.php:131). The toggle uses a confirmation modal with no wire:confirm (queues.blade.php:145-164). Serve.php handles no selection -> serve_empty (:69-73), catches InactiveQueue/NoWaitingTickets, lets AuthorizationException through, rate-limits successful calls (:79-99) and lists waiting tickets in call order with a 30-item cap (:131-158). Members tabs: setActiveTab whitelist (Members.php:70-75) and role="tablist", with the invite form only on the invites tab (members.blade.php:6-19). Routes are added (web.php:59-60), navbar links gated by role (default-page.blade.php:49-56), and every lang key exists in both locales.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through CreateQueue/UpdateQueue/SetQueueAccess/CallNextTicket. Authorization uses policies (authorize('create', [Queue::class, $entity]), Gate::allows('call')). CHANGELOG and docs/business-rules.md are updated. Two deviations: Queues `name`/`renameName` have no #[Validate] (Queues.php:31,49), and several public actions (create, rename, toggleActive, grant/revokeAccess) do not call $this->authorize themselves, relying on authorization inside the actions. The row and modal markup in queues.blade.php and serve.blade.php is inline rather than extracted into Blade components.

security.evidence: Every client id is resolved scoped (`$this->entity->queues()->findOrFail(...)`, `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail(...)`). entity and lastCalledTicketId are #[Locked]. mode is validated with `in:any,priority_only,normal_only`. Render degrades to empty data for a demoted manager (Queues.php:222-231). Output is escaped with {{ }} throughout. Remaining gaps have limited impact: there is no component-level authorize in create/rename/toggleActive/setAccess (the actions authorize, and tests cover 403), and the free-text fields have no #[Validate].

tests.evidence: QueuesTest.php and ServeTest.php cover happy paths, domain errors, foreign-id tamper tests for every action ('renaming a foreign queue through a tampered editingQueueId', 'a tampered accessQueueId ... discloses nothing'), a forbidden dataset over all 9 actions after demotion, the audit-log mock, the mode tamper, the locked lastCalledTicketId, and rate limiting including 'failed calls do not burn the rate limit'. The navbar and the lang-key parity are tested too. Existing members tests were adapted to the tabs, not weakened.

simplicity.evidence: The surfaceDomainErrors helper (Queues.php:200-213) avoids repeating try/catch, and resetNested centralizes the state reset. The code is mostly lean. One small piece of duplication: the demoted-manager branch in render repeats the view-data shape, and the status tag markup appears twice in queues.blade.php.

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods small. PHPDoc explains the untrusted state ('Untrusted client state — always re-resolved scoped to the entity'). Style matches the members page. The test helper callExpectingNotFound with `expect(true)->toBeTrue()` in a catch is a little awkward. The Blade views use long inline style attributes.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: components, views, routes, lang, navbar, members tabs, docs/CHANGELOG and tests. The extra serve_rate_limited key and the lang-parity test are directly related.

issues.explanation: Public input properties `name` and `renameName` have no #[Validate] and validate() is never called. The project's Livewire policy requires this, even though the domain action also validates.

toggleActive, create, rename and setAccess do not call $this->authorize in the component and rely only on the action's internal authorization. Rule 3 of the Livewire policy asks for authorization inside each public method.
waitingTickets does not filter on is_active, so a selectedQueueId pointing at an inactive (but callable) queue still lists its tickets, while the selector only offers active queues.
toggleActive does not require confirmingToggle, so the confirmation step can be skipped by calling the method directly. Its impact is only UX because authorization still applies.
The active/inactive tag and the modal-card skeletons are repeated inline instead of extracted into anonymous Blade components.
callExpectingNotFound swallows exceptions with a placeholder `expect(true)->toBeTrue()`. Asserting the exception explicitly would read more clearly.

review.summary: The change adds the Queues management page, the Serve panel, members tabs, navbar links, translations and docs. It calls the domain actions and resolves every client id scoped to the entity, which meets the full contract. Tests are thorough, with tamper, unauthorized and rate-limit cases. Remaining points are minor convention gaps (#[Validate] on the name fields, component-level authorize in some actions) and a small edge case for inactive selected queues, so this is approvable with nits.
